sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:141830
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 8283 of 2019

Applicant :- Gulshan
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Neeraj Kumar Srivastava,Amrita Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Sanjay Kumar Mishra, Advocate holding brief of Ms. Amrita Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Suresh Bahadur Singh, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 267 of 2012, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Masoori,
District Ghaziabad during pendency of the trial.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that this is third bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and earlier two bail applications of the applicant were dismissed for want of prosecution and applicant is in jail since 03.04.2012 i.e. for more than 11 years and till date neither trial could be concluded nor his bail application could be decided on merit.
He further submits that applicant is husband of the deceased, however, he is pressing the instant bail application mainly on the ground of long incarceration of the applicant of more than 11 years.

He further submits that there is dying declaration of the deceased on record, which has been annexed along with instant application and according to dying declaration of the deceased, she stated that applicant ablazed her but her dying Gulshan vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132911855/
1
declaration appears to be unreliable and till date its sanctity could not be proved.
He further submits that in the dying declaration, deceased did not make any allegation of demand of dowry.

He further submits that considering the long incarceration of the applicant of more than 11 years, applicant,
who is although husband of the deceased, may be enlarged on bail.
4. Per contra, learned AGA although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that applicant is in jail since 03.04.2012 i.e. for more than 11 years.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

6. Although, applicant is husband of the deceased and in the dying declaration deceased also stated against him but considering the fact that applicant is in jail since 03.04.2012 i.e. for more than 11 years, in my view, applicant may be released on bail.

7. Therefore, considering the long incarceration of the applicant of more than 11 years, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
8. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

9. However, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, trial court is directed to conclude the trial within six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order or communication of this order strictly as per provisions of Section 309 Cr.P.C., if there is no legal impediment.

10. Let the applicant - Gulshan be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
11. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

12. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
